scenario.title: Cash flow planning

scenario.help: Starting cash is entered by you, not read from a bank. On schedule assumes all dated receivables arrive in full and all payables are paid on time. Your scenario delays and scales receivables, keeps payables on time, and adds extra costs at each 30-day checkpoint. Amounts include recorded tax. This calculation stays in your browser and does not change the ledger.
scenario.excluded: {count} overdue or undated items are excluded: {incoming} incoming and {outgoing} outgoing. Confirm their dates before including them.

scenario.openingHelp: Enter it yourself; no bank connection. Enter 0 to see only the cash movement.
scenario.delayHelp: Applies to all included receipts. Payments you owe keep their recorded dates.
scenario.collectionHelp: 100 means full payment; 80 means only 80% of each receipt is collected. This is an assumption, not a likelihood estimate.
scenario.extraHelp: Extra spending beyond recorded payables. Deducted once per 30-day checkpoint; do not include it twice.
scenario.invalid: Check the amounts and enter a collection percentage between 0 and 100.

partners.intro: Built from the signed projects each organization is the client of, and their payments. The on-time rate counts received payments — it isn't a credit score for the company.

partners.methodBody: Projects count signed ones, archived included, and leave out negotiations. Voided entries and costs don't count. A deposit and a balance count as two payments; average days late looks only at payments received late. A payment not yet due isn't late.

musician.0: Arena dreams, one song at a time. Make something you love today. Your to-dos are right here.
musician.1: That demo can take another draft. A melody you love is worth the extra time.
musician.2: Whatever the crowd size, today's show deserves your sound. Make it yours.
musician.3: Headphones on, world turned down. Leave a little room for your own music today.
musician.4: Record that idea before it slips away. A great song can start with a voice note.
musician.5: Give that tricky section another listen today. The next chord might be the one.

manager.0: You're keeping a lot of people on track. Save a slot in the schedule for your own lunch, too.
manager.1: One email, one next step. You don't have to hold the whole day in your head.
manager.2: The work you do backstage gives someone room to shine out front. That matters.
manager.3: A confirmed date or a settled detail counts as progress. Give yourself credit for it.
manager.4: Let's get the day in order. When there's a break, take it—and have some water.
manager.5: Good partnerships need someone connecting the dots. One clear next step at a time.

video.0: Make room for a shot you love today. Not every frame has to start with a brief.
video.1: Stuck on an edit? Step away for a bit. Fresh eyes can find the cut.
video.2: Get the first cut out, then shape it. Today doesn't have to be the final export.
video.3: Some frames are worth waiting for. The light, rhythm, and details you notice become part of the work.
video.4: Charge the batteries, feed the crew—and yourself. You're part of the kit that needs looking after.
video.5: Pick one unfinished idea from that drive. You only need to move it a little further today.

influencer.0: Make something you'd want to watch today. Your life is bigger than the analytics tab.
influencer.1: Not every post has to go viral. Helping someone find something they love counts, too.
influencer.2: No ideas yet? Go live a little. Sometimes the next post finds you along the way.
influencer.3: Take your time choosing partnerships. The right fit leaves room for your own voice.
influencer.4: Share it your way. Your particular angle is part of what people come for.
influencer.5: Filmed, edited, posted—that's real work. Take a break before checking the numbers again.

model.0: Bring yourself to the frame today. You don't have to look like someone else to belong in it.
model.1: One casting isn't the whole story. Look after yourself; there will be other rooms to walk into.
model.2: Find your own pace today. That moment when you feel at ease can come through on camera.
model.3: Early call time? Have something to eat before you go. You deserve a comfortable start.
model.4: Every shoot is a chance to learn something about yourself. Try an expression that feels new to you.
model.5: When you wrap, let your shoulders drop. Showing up in front of the camera takes work.

other.0: Start with one thing that matters to you. A little progress still counts.
other.1: Your pace doesn't have to match anyone else's. Take your own next step today.
other.2: Some ideas need time to grow. Leave a little space for the one that isn't quite ready yet.
other.3: If the list feels long, choose one thing that matters most. Then take it from there.
other.4: There's a life outside the work, too. Save a little time for it today.
other.5: You don't have to feel certain to begin. A small experiment is a good start.

assistantCosts.title: Assistant usage and pricing
assistantCosts.intro: Local evaluation · USD · Text assistant inference only. Choose a test to compare usage and inspect every exchange.
assistantCosts.planNotice: Pricing hypotheses: Basic US$20/month and Pro US$40/month. One AI reply counts once, including each follow-up. Local lookups would not consume the AI allowance. These plan limits are not implemented.
assistantCosts.rangeNote: Full allowance used every day. Monthly min–max repeats the cheapest or most expensive observed AI reply; it is a scenario estimate, not a guaranteed bound. Changing the evaluation changes these estimates.
assistantCosts.guardTitle: How to make the maximum enforceable
assistantCosts.guardNote: Proposed per-request cap: 6,000 input tokens including instructions, context and history; 1,500 output tokens including reasoning. At current prices, charging all input at the higher cache-write rate gives US$0.0015/reply: Basic US$1.35 and Pro US$4.50 per 30 days. Add monthly inference budgets of US$1.50 / US$5, count retries and incomplete responses, and reserve cost before sending. These safeguards are proposals, not active plan enforcement.
assistantCosts.currentGuard: The local experiment currently has a shared US$5 cap and broad byte-based input bounds. Its conservative maximum reservation is US$0.026262/request with 1,500 output tokens. A daily message count alone cannot guarantee the proposed monthly cost.
assistantCosts.scopeNote: Excludes Gmail ingestion, embeddings, attachments, database/hosting, payment fees, support, taxes and acquisition. This is not a total operating-cost or profit estimate. The US$20/40 prices need customer validation.
assistantCosts.projection: {daily} AI replies/day ≈ {dayTokens} tokens and {dayCost}/day. Over 30 days: {monthly} replies, {tokens} tokens, {cost}. Repeating the observed 95th-percentile cost: {p95}/month.
assistantCosts.question: Question and answer
assistantCosts.method: Daily: 100 independent exchanges, including 40 local lookups and 60 AI questions. Follow-up: 20 conversations × 5 exchanges, using the actual prior responses with the same latest-8-message history window as the app. Includes short drafts, negotiation, contract questions, ambiguous/adversarial requests and longer briefs. Synthetic fixtures dated 2026-10-07; no customer messages. Uses the app router, context and OpenAI adapter, but bypasses UI authentication and daily-rate-limit plumbing. This measures usage, not UI load or response-quality certification.
assistantCosts.accounting: Input/output counts come from API usage. Reasoning is already included in output; cached reads/writes are subsets of input. Local replies use zero model tokens. USD values are estimates, not invoices. Failed or unknown usage remains reserved in the shared ledger and is not silently counted as free.
assistantCosts.comparison: The two older runs called AI for all 100 cases. They are retained for comparison but are not pooled with the new runs: prompts, routing and case mix differ. Small synthetic samples cannot establish real customer usage percentiles.
assistantCosts.rates: gpt-6-luna · low reasoning · standard tier · 1,500 output-token cap. Verified 2026-10-08: per million tokens, input US$0.10; cached read US$0.01; cache write US$0.125; output US$0.50.
